name: Long-Context Prompting
question: How do I get reliable answers from a very long prompt?
summary: How to prompt when the input is hundreds of pages: documents first, each wrapped in tags with its source, the question and instructions last, and a request to quote the relevant passages before answering. Long prompts are slow and expensive, so the shared prefix is cached, and retrieval is still the better choice when questions need only a few passages. Models also attend less reliably to the middle of very long inputs, so test on real multi-hop questions, not just needle-in-a-haystack checks.
useCases: Questions that span many parts of one long file: a loan bundle, a contract set, an annual report
Analysts asking many questions over the same documents
Multi-hop questions that retrieval of a few chunks tends to miss

items.detail: long inputs at the top, the question at the end
each document in tags with source, date and page range
ask for the relevant quotes, then the answer from them
cache the shared prefix so later questions cost a fraction
facts buried mid-context are found less reliably
compare accuracy and cost against retrieving the top chunks

steps: Put long documents at the top, each in tags with its source and pages
Put the question and instructions at the end
Ask for the relevant quotes first, then an answer based only on them
Cache the document prefix, and compare with retrieval on your own multi-hop questions
pitfalls: Question at the top of 2,00,000 tokens of documents
Paying full input price for the same documents on every question
Trusting a needle-in-a-haystack score as proof of multi-hop reasoning
remember: Documents first, question last, quotes before answers.
caption: Illustrative: Kosh Finance, a fictional NBFC, asks 50 questions over a 400-page loan bundle.

code.text: for i, d in enumerate(bundle, start=1))
system=[{"type": "text", "text": "You answer questions about a loan file."}],
"First copy the clauses that matter into <quotes>, with document "
"index and page. Then answer in <answer> using only those quotes. "
"If they do not settle it, say so.\n\n"
out = ask("Which prepayment charge applies after the 2025 addendum?")
check_quotes_exist(out, bundle)          # every quote must be found verbatim

steps.title: Put the documents first, tagged
steps.text: Each document goes in its own tags with its source file and page range, all above the question. The model can then say where a fact came from.

steps.title: Ask the question last
steps.text: A question placed after the documents is answered noticeably better than one placed before 2,50,000 tokens of text.

steps.title: Quote before answering
steps.text: The model first copies the clauses that matter into quotes, then answers from them alone. It cuts through the noise and leaves evidence you can check.

steps.title: Cache the document prefix
steps.text: Marking the documents for caching means the next 49 questions read them from cache at about a tenth of the input price, and much faster.

steps.title: Check the quotes exist
steps.text: Code confirms each quote appears in the cited document. A quote that cannot be found flags an invented clause.

steps.title: Compare with retrieval
steps.text: On your own questions, measure stuffing against retrieving the top chunks. Here stuffing wins on multi-hop questions; retrieval is cheaper for single facts.

pros: Handles questions that span many distant parts of a file
Caching makes repeated questions over the same documents cheap
No chunking or index to build for a one-off analysis
cons: The first call is slow and expensive
Recall of facts buried mid-context is less reliable
Context limits cap how much fits
Every question pays for all the text unless cached
avoidWhen: Most questions need one or two passages from a large, changing corpus (use retrieval)
A single short answer per document set, where caching cannot pay off

practice.scenario: Kosh Finance, a fictional NBFC, lets credit analysts ask questions over a 400-page loan bundle: the agreement, sanction letters and a 2025 addendum. The documents go first in the prompt, each in tags with its source and pages; the question goes last; the model quotes the clauses it relies on before answering. The document prefix is cached, so after the first question each one costs about a tenth.

industries.use: Questions across agreements, sanction letters and addenda for one borrower
Clause lookups across a contract and its amendments
Questions over an annual report, earnings call transcripts and filings

practice.analogy: Handing a reviewer the whole file with the question clipped to the last page, and asking them to flag the paragraphs before giving an opinion.

library.name: Anthropic Python SDK
library.what: Messages API with prompt caching via cache_control on a content block; usage shows cached and uncached input tokens.

practice.note: load_bundle is a stub. Check current model names, context limits and caching prices in the provider documentation.

samples.code:
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()
bundle = load_bundle("loan_UL-5521")      # list of (name, pages, text)

docs = "\n".join(f'<document index="{i}" source="{n}" pages="{p}">\n{t}\n</document>'
                 for i, (n, p, t) in enumerate(bundle, start=1))

def ask(question: str) -> str:
    msg = client.messages.create(
        model="claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens=1500,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": f"<documents>\n{docs}\n</documents>",
             "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}},
            {"type": "text", "text": "Quote the relevant clauses in <quotes> with document index "
             "and page, then answer in <answer> using only those quotes.\n\n"
             f"Question: {question}"}]}])
    print("cached:", msg.usage.cache_read_input_tokens, "new:", msg.usage.input_tokens)
    return msg.content[0].text

print(ask("Which prepayment charge applies after the 2025 addendum?"))

numericDrill.question: A 2,50,000-token bundle costs ₹0.25 per 1,000 input tokens, and cached reads cost a tenth. Over 50 questions with caching (the first question pays in full), what is the average input cost per question in rupees?
numericDrill.answer: First question ₹62.5; the other 49 pay ₹6.25 each = ₹306.25. Total ₹368.75 ÷ 50 = ₹7.375 a question, against ₹62.5 without caching.

interview.question: How would you prompt a model over a 300-page contract?
interview.answer: Put the contract first, split into tagged documents with source and page ranges, and the question last. Ask for the relevant quotes before the answer, and verify the quotes exist. Cache the prefix if several questions will be asked, and compare with retrieval on real multi-hop questions.

interview.question: When is retrieval better than a long context?
interview.answer: When questions need a few passages from a large or changing corpus, when cost and latency per call matter, or when the documents exceed the context window. Long context wins when questions span many parts of one file and many questions share it.

mistakes.mistake: Putting the question above the documents
mistakes.fix: Place documents first and the question at the end

mistakes.mistake: Re-sending the same documents at full price

quiz.question: Where should the question go in a prompt with 2,00,000 tokens of documents?
quiz.explanation: Long-context questions are answered better when they follow the documents.

quiz.question: Why ask the model to quote clauses before answering?
options: The answer rests on checkable evidence and the model focuses on what matters
Quotes are required by the API
quiz.explanation: Quoting first focuses attention and gives you evidence to verify.

quiz.question: A 2,50,000-token prefix costs ₹62.5 per question. Cached reads cost a tenth. What do 10 questions cost with caching (first pays in full)?
Which help a model use a long policy bundle well? Select all that apply.
options: Each document in tags with source and pages
Removing all headings from the documents
quiz.explanation: Headings help the model navigate; removing them hurts.

quiz.question: What does "lost in the middle" describe?
options: Facts in the middle of a long context used less reliably than those at the ends
quiz.explanation: Position within a long context affects how reliably information is used.

quiz.question: A needle-in-a-haystack test scores 99%. What does it not prove?
options: That the model can read long inputs
That it can combine several distant facts to answer multi-hop questions
That the context window is large
quiz.explanation: Finding one planted sentence differs from reasoning across many passages.

quiz.question: When is retrieval usually better than putting everything in the prompt?
options: A few passages answer each question from a large, changing corpus
Every question spans the whole file
There are many questions on one file
quiz.explanation: Retrieval is cheaper and faster when only a few passages matter.

quiz.question: Prompt caching needs what to be true of the prefix?
options: It must be identical across calls
It must be at the end
quiz.explanation: Caching matches an identical prefix; a question placed first breaks it.

quiz.question: Quotes in an answer do not appear in the source. What should the system do?
quiz.explanation: A quote that cannot be found indicates an invented clause.

quiz.question: Which are costs of very long prompts? Select all that apply.
options: Less reliable use of facts mid-context
quiz.explanation: Citations are not automatic; they must be asked for.

quiz.question: An analyst asks 30 questions about one annual report. What cuts cost the most?
quiz.explanation: Repeated questions over the same prefix benefit most from caching.

quiz.question: Retrieval gets 90% of single-fact questions but 56% of multi-hop ones. What explains the gap?
options: Multi-hop answers need passages that often miss the top-k
The embedding model is too large
quiz.explanation: Several distant passages rarely all make a small top-k.

quiz.question: What should each document tag include?
options: Source name and page range, so answers can cite them
quiz.explanation: Metadata lets answers point to where a fact came from.

quiz.question: A 600-page notification set exceeds the context window. What now?
options: Retrieve relevant sections, or split into parts and combine answers
quiz.explanation: Beyond the window, retrieval or map-reduce is required.

quiz.question: Accuracy rises from 80% to 89% after quoting first. On 50 questions, how many more are right?
quiz.explanation: 9 points of 50 questions is 4.5 more correct answers.

quiz.question: Which belong in an evaluation of long-context prompting? Select all that apply.
options: Multi-hop questions from your own documents
Checks that quotes exist in the source
quiz.explanation: Synthetic needle tests alone miss real failure modes.

quiz.question: Where should instructions like "answer only from the quotes" go?
options: At the very top, before the documents
After the documents, next to the question
quiz.explanation: Instructions near the question, after the documents, are followed more reliably.

quiz.question: Why tag documents instead of pasting them as one block?
options: The model can tell documents apart and cite them
quiz.explanation: Clear boundaries help the model keep sources separate.

quiz.question: Cached input costs a tenth. If uncached input is ₹60 per question, what does a cached question cost for input?
A team places the question first to "prime" the model. What is the side effect with caching?
options: The prefix changes every call, so nothing is cached
quiz.explanation: A varying first block breaks prefix caching.
